title: ACA s. 8 — Power to refer parties to arbitration where agreement exists (ACA s. 8)

content.overview: Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 requires a judicial authority seized of an action concerning a matter covered by an arbitration agreement to refer the parties to arbitration when a party to the agreement, or a person claiming through or under that party, applies in time, unless the authority finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists.
content.glance: Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 requires a judicial authority seized of an action concerning a matter covered by an arbitration agreement to refer the parties to arbitration when a party to the agreement, or a person claiming through or under that party, applies in time, unless the authority finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists.
content.study:
Section 8 — Power to refer parties to arbitration where there is an arbitration agreement

Section 8 operates when a judicial authority is seized of an action concerning a matter that is the subject of an arbitration agreement.

Under section 8(1), the statutory conditions are cumulative in structure:
1. an action is before a judicial authority;
2. the action concerns a matter that is the subject of an arbitration agreement;
3. a party to the arbitration agreement, or a person claiming through or under that party, makes the application;
4. the application is made not later than the date of submitting the applicant's first statement on the substance of the dispute; and
5. the judicial authority does not find prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists.

The consequence is referral to arbitration when the statutory conditions are met.

Section 8(2) imposes a documentary requirement: the application must be accompanied by the original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy. Its proviso addresses the situation where the original or certified copy is retained by the other party: the applicant may file a copy with a petition requesting the Court to call upon that party to produce the original or certified copy.

Section 8(3) makes clear that the pendency of the section 8 application does not prevent commencement or continuation of arbitration or the making of an arbitral award.

The present statutory threshold is deliberately framed as prima facie: the judicial authority does not conduct the final merits determination of the arbitration agreement at this stage. The section must be applied to the statutory text and the particular procedural record.

sections.heading: 1. Triggering action and arbitration agreement
sections.body: Section 8 applies where an action is brought before a judicial authority in a matter that is the subject of an arbitration agreement. The court must first identify the arbitration agreement and the overlap between the agreement and the subject matter of the action.

sections.heading: 2. Who may apply and when
sections.body: The application may be made by a party to the arbitration agreement or a person claiming through or under such party. It must be made not later than the date of submitting the applicant's first statement on the substance of the dispute.

sections.heading: 3. Prima facie validity threshold
sections.body: The statutory direction is to refer unless the judicial authority finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists. The section therefore sets a threshold inquiry rather than a full adjudication of every merits issue concerning the dispute.

sections.heading: 4. Arbitration agreement document
sections.body: Section 8(2) requires the application to be accompanied by the original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy. The proviso provides a route where the original or certified copy is retained by the other party.

sections.heading: 5. Arbitration may proceed
sections.body: Under section 8(3), the pendency of the section 8 application does not itself prevent arbitration from being commenced or continued or an arbitral award from being made.

sections.heading: 6. Application sequence
sections.body: Counsel should identify the action, the arbitration agreement, the statutory applicant, the timing of the application, the documentary requirement, and the prima facie validity threshold before addressing the consequence of referral.

provisions.title: Power to refer parties to arbitration where there is an arbitration agreement

examples.title: Timely referral application
examples.body: A civil action concerns a dispute expressly covered by an arbitration agreement. A party to that agreement applies before submitting its first statement on the substance of the dispute and establishes the required documentary foundation. Section 8's referral mechanism is engaged, subject to the prima facie validity threshold.

examples.title: Late application
examples.body: A party waits until after submitting its first statement on the substance of the dispute before applying under section 8. The statutory timing requirement is not satisfied.

examples.title: Prima facie invalid agreement
examples.body: The judicial authority finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists. Section 8(1) does not require referral in that circumstance.

examples.title: Original agreement unavailable
examples.body: The applicant does not possess the original or duly certified copy because the other party retains it. The section 8(2) proviso provides a mechanism to file a copy and request production of the original or certified copy.

hypotheticals.question: A defendant files a section 8 application after submitting its first statement on the substance of the dispute. Is the statutory timing requirement met?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 8(1) requires the application not later than the date of submitting the applicant's first statement on the substance of the dispute.

hypotheticals.question: The arbitration agreement is retained by the opposing party. Can the applicant still invoke section 8(2)?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The proviso to section 8(2) addresses that situation and permits the applicant to file a copy with a petition asking the Court to call upon the other party to produce the original or duly certified copy.

hypotheticals.question: Does a pending section 8 application automatically stop an arbitration already commenced?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 8(3) expressly provides that arbitration may be commenced or continued and an arbitral award may be made notwithstanding the pending application.

hypotheticals.question: Must the judicial authority finally decide every disputed question about validity before referring the parties?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 8(1) states a prima facie threshold: referral is required unless the authority finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists. The final legal consequences must therefore not be overstated as a full merits adjudication under section 8.

misconceptions.trap: Any party can apply under section 8 at any time before judgment.
misconceptions.correction: The applicant must be a party to the arbitration agreement or a person claiming through or under such party, and the application must be made no later than the applicant's first statement on the substance of the dispute.

misconceptions.trap: Section 8 always requires the court to conduct a full trial on the arbitration agreement.
misconceptions.correction: Section 8(1) states a prima facie threshold for the judicial authority's validity inquiry.

misconceptions.trap: Failure to possess the original arbitration agreement automatically defeats the application.
misconceptions.correction: Section 8(2)'s proviso provides a production mechanism where the original or certified copy is retained by the other party.

misconceptions.trap: A pending section 8 application automatically stays arbitration.
misconceptions.correction: Section 8(3) expressly permits arbitration to commence or continue and an award to be made while the application is pending.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the statutory test under section 8?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify a judicial action concerning a matter subject to an arbitration agreement; establish that the applicant is a party or claims through or under a party; confirm that the application was made no later than the applicant's first statement on the substance of the dispute; satisfy section 8(2)'s documentary requirement; and address whether the authority finds prima facie that no valid arbitration agreement exists.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: If the statutory conditions are satisfied, section 8 directs referral to arbitration.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should counsel frame a section 8 referral application?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Begin with the arbitration agreement and identify the overlap with the court action. Prove the applicant's statutory standing and the timing of the application. File the original or duly certified copy, or invoke the section 8(2) proviso where the other party retains it. Address the prima facie validity threshold and conclude with the statutory referral consequence. Section 8(3) should be addressed if the arbitral process is already underway.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Keep the statutory referral mechanism separate from merits of the underlying dispute.
